about.title: Yountville Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Yountville is a small town, but its roads carry a steady stream of visitor and commuter traffic through wine country. Public records show injury collisions here, most clustering on Wednesday afternoons between 2 and 4 p.m., often along SR-29, Washington Street, and California Drive corridors where local traffic mixes with tourists unfamiliar with the roads. Whether you were stopped at a light on Washington Street or merging near Rt 29, the aftermath of a crash can feel overwhelming: medical appointments, missed work, an insurance adjuster calling before you've even seen a doctor. We handle car accident claims for injured people in Yountville and can evaluate your situation. There's no obligation, and no fee unless we recover compensation on your behalf.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before Talking to the Insurer

items.title: California's Clock Is Ticking
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a car accident claim in California, but that window can shrink to as little as six months if a government entity — like Napa County or the City of Yountville — is involved. We can help you figure out which deadline applies before you lose the chance to act.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Work Against You
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, meaning your compensation can be reduced by whatever percentage you're found responsible for the crash. Anything you say in a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer could be used to shift blame onto you, so it's worth having guidance before that call.

items.title: No Cap Means Documentation Matters
items.desc: California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering, but proving those losses depends on solid evidence — medical records, photos, witness accounts — gathered early. Our team can help make sure that evidence isn't lost or overlooked in the days after your crash.

items.question: Should I give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: It's usually best to avoid giving a recorded statement until you've spoken with an attorney. Insurance adjusters are trained to ask questions that can shift fault under California's comparative negligence rules, and even an innocent-sounding answer can be used against you later. We can advise you on what, if anything, to say.

items.question: What if my accident happened on Rt 29 or another state highway near Yountville?
items.answer: Crashes on state highways like SR-29 can sometimes involve claims against a government entity responsible for road design or maintenance, which comes with a much shorter filing deadline — sometimes just six months. It's worth having an attorney review the location and circumstances quickly so you don't miss that window.

items.question: How much does it cost to talk to an attorney?
items.answer: Nothing. Our consultations are free, and we work on contingency, meaning we only get paid if you recover compensation. There's no upfront cost and no obligation to move forward after your consultation.
